blocks.text: Cedar Hills Homes for Sale | Surrey BC MLS

parts.t: Cedar Hills is a quiet pocket of North Surrey between Scott Road and King George, south of 100 Avenue. It's mostly detached houses, many with suites, on streets that feel more settled than the City Centre blocks to the east. These are the homes for sale in Cedar Hills now.

I've been licensed since 2015 and have more than $500M in sales behind me. I grew up on a Langley farm and moved back there, so I know how much the drive, the yard and the school run matter when you pick a street. Read my
Cedar Hills neighbourhood guide
or compare all
North Surrey homes for sale
Written by
Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®

Cedar Hills Elementary is on 98 Avenue and Prince Charles Elementary is on 100 Avenue. L.A. Matheson is the secondary for much of the area. Catchments follow the address, so look it up in the Surrey Schools School Locator.
Robson Park, at 12678 100 Avenue, has more than 5 hectares of open space. Moffat Memorial Park on 122 Street is another local spot.
Routes 316 and 321 run near the neighbourhood and connect to SkyTrain at Surrey Central and Scott Road.

Cedar Hills tends to suit buyers who want a detached house with a suite to help with the mortgage, or a home big enough for extended family. Streets are quiet, lots are a decent size, and you're between two major roads without living right on them.
It may suit you less if you want to walk to SkyTrain every day. You'll be on a bus for that part of the trip.

For many Cedar Hills homes, the suite is a big part of the value. If yours was built with permits, have those papers ready. If it wasn't, talk to me before you list so we can price and describe it honestly. I'd rather you hear the hard questions from me than from a buyer's lawyer.

When you call, tell me the street, the price range and how many bedrooms you need. I'll send matching listings and point out anything I'd want to know before booking a showing. If a home has been on the market a while, I'll tell you what I think is holding it back.

blocks.text: What to check in a Cedar Hills house

parts.t: Many homes here were built decades ago and some have been added onto. That's fine, but the paperwork matters.
Ask whether any suite was built with permits
Check the roof, the drain tiles and the electrical panel
Confirm the zone with the City before you plan a rebuild or more units
Walk the street at school drop-off time

blocks.text: Which elementary schools are in Cedar Hills?

parts.t: Cedar Hills Elementary on 98 Avenue and Prince Charles Elementary on 100 Avenue. Check the School Locator for the address.

blocks.text: What high school serves Cedar Hills?

parts.t: L.A. Matheson serves much of the area, but confirm the catchment for the exact address.
Robson Park, at 12678 100 Avenue, with more than 5 hectares.

blocks.text: Do many Cedar Hills homes have suites?

parts.t: Many do. Ask for the permit history, because only a suite built with permits counts as legal.

blocks.text: Is Cedar Hills a good fit for a multi-generational family?

parts.t: Many homes have the space and a suite. Check the permit history and the zone before you plan how the home will be used.

blocks.text: Is Cedar Hills close to SkyTrain?

parts.t: Not walking distance for most homes. Routes 316 and 321 connect to the stations.
